notes.title: Update 2015.04.26: Nothing Ventured...
notes.content:
[img]http://i.imgur.com/u6Dx9Ko.gif[/img]
I made an announcement about big upcoming changes last night, thinking that I would hold off a couple more days before updating, but after knocking out a few more big changes and features today, I started thinking, "Well, now I'll either have to hold off for more Extra Beta testing, or I can just bite the bullet and push it all out now." I have opted for the latter.

What's the point of Early Access if I can't majorly screw with everyone's copy of the game whenever the whim strikes anyway?

There are some daunting patch notes below (and they're the abridged version!), but here are the highlights:
[list]
[*]New matching mechanics
[*]New item mechanics
[*]A pause feature
[*]A score multiplier that increases over time, but resets when you pause the game
[*]Fear rewrite (fearful heroes will drop out of battles and retreat from your dungeon)
[*]Codex changes (e.g., you can drag the codex around to reposition it now)
[*]Lots of additional fixes and adjustments
[/list]

Please let me know what you think of the changes, and report any of the inevitable bugs in the discussion forums! Thank you =)!

[Edit: Updated to 2015.04.27 to fix the Bomb description, remove Punji traps on floor item changes, and prevent duplicate usables from being spawned.]

[Edit 2: Updated to 2015.04.27b to fix a rare crash and make some minor adjustments.]

[h1]Changelog[/h1]
[b]Additions:[/b][list]
[*]Ability to pause (spacebar or on-screen button)
[*]Score multiplier that increases over time (up to x1.5), but drops back to x1 when you pause
[*]Hovering ghost icon on fearful characters
[*]Added a comma to the multiplier font, for regions where it replaces a period in denoting decimal places
[*]Added codex icon that can be clicked to open the codex, or dragged/dropped on things to open to a relevant entry
[/list]
[b]Changes:[/b][list]
[*]Matching mechanics have changed significantly, allowing for vertical slides and multiple slides per move (four, by default)
[*]Item mechanics have changed significantly, making items re-usable with a cooldown, and sorting items into distinct Usable/Deployable/Passive categories
[*]Floors can now have a deployed item, which will automatically be used when appropriate (and pending a cooldown); assigning a new item will replace the old one
[*]Items that are usable on the Hoard no longer target specific tiles; you just click to use them
[*]Calcifier, Bomb, and 'Sploder are no longer usable on floors
[*]Greater Grasp now increases number of slides allowed per move by two
[*]Portable Punji can now be used on floors that already have traps
[*]Calcifier, 'Sploder, and Mit now "spread" their resource types; any Hoard tiles of their type will randomly infect adjacent tiles
[*]Magnet now immediately sucks up all gear and scrap tiles from the Hoard
[*]Bomb now destroys the top four rows of your Hoard; it does not collect tiles, but it is useful for quickly clearing room for another floor
[*]Reduced item drop rate
[*]Items no longer stack
[*]All items have a type: tool, device, potion, relic, explosive, or artifact
[*]Can no longer purchase items
[*]"Shop" floors now decrease cooldowns for specific categories of items (for example, the Alchemist reduces potion cooldowns by 10 seconds)
[*]Can no longer sell items to Fence by dropping them over that floor (doubt anyone was doing this anyway)
[*]Fenced items now refund their full value
[*]Fenced value is now displayed in the "recycle bin" where you fence items
[*]Fearful heroes will now retreat from you dungeon without engaging your minions (they should still trigger traps, however)
[*]Potion effects no longer stack (this prevents a dormant floor--such as the Sanctum--from benefiting from many item cooldown cycles)
[*]Changed the way fatigue is calculated for characters with buffed defense, allowing defense to be re-buffed (this helps offset the effect-stacking change)
[*]Some tutorial revisions
[*]The codex can now be dragged to reposition it on the screen
[*]A number of display and language changes in the Codex
[*]Many other UI changes and adjustments[/list]
[b]Fixes:[/b][list]
[*]"Background text" wouldn't always appear on Codex entries (this is the fake text blocks that surround the actual text and images)
[*]Some splash and shard particles were not behaving appropriately
[*]Assassin backstabs were sometimes broken
[*]There was a *very* brief visual glitch when tiles were collected
[*]Smoothed out some tile motion
[*]Icons on popups wouldn't always move smoothly with the popup
[*]Some Hoard effects were not mirrored on the dedicated Hoard view[/list]

notes.title: Major Changes Incoming!
notes.content:
[img]http://i.imgur.com/52HteQN.gif[/img]
Last week, I began offering a separate beta build for Tomb of Tyrants; I know that technically the game as a whole is already in beta, but now you can test [i]extra beta[/i] features and changes by checking out the "Betas" tab under the game's Preferences in Steam.

It's been a little while since the last main release (a [i]long[/i] while compared to previous update gaps that averaged about half a week), and while I'll admit that some of that delay is due to an onslaught of escalating personal obligations, a lot of it is because I've been trying to improve some of the game's core mechanics, which has required a lot of playing and experimenting on my own.

But now you can help! By testing out Extra Beta 2015.04.25 and leaving your feedback (in [url=http://steamcommunity.com/app/340360/discussions/0/610575007204564803/]this thread[/url] or with me directly), you can help me polish up or further revamp some of what I've been working on for the last three weeks.

The two biggest things going on here are big changes to matching and item usage.

[h1]Matching Changes:[/h1]
Instead of grabbing entire rows and moving them left/right, you now grab individual pieces, which you can shift left/right [b]or up/down[/b]! This works similarly to the old mechanics, where tiles wrap around, but now you can slide columns and even make multiple slides per move (up to 4), giving you much more control over the Hoard; you can target the resources you actually want, more easily set up large matches, and feel really clever when you do!

I feel that this is more engaging than the old mechanic, because it allows you to spend less time matching, prevents deadlock situations, and yet still allows for the tactics you may have grown accustomed to. However, the point of this testing (and, indeed, Early Access in general) is to find out if this is actually really fun and balanced!

[h1]Item Changes:[/h1]
Usable items are now all re-usable with cooldowns. Instead of using items once on a floor, you now deploy them to a floor, and that floor will then re-use the item regularly. Items that affect the Hoard can simply be clicked to used, as they no longer target specific tiles. Items that previously affected either the Hoard or floors have been changed to only affect the Hoard (so no more using bombs on enemies--although some other item may very well be introduced to fill this role later =).

The goal here was to simplify, and you'll see fewer items in general, because you get more out of the items you receive. This should prevent the inventory from becoming cumbersomely cluttered with stacks of items that you feel pressured to find a use for. You can no longer purchase items, but floors that previously sold them now reduce cooldowns for specific classes of items (for example, the Acrid Alchemist reduces all potion cooldowns by 10 seconds).

I plan to push these changes out in a major release in the next couple of days, but I would love to hear more feedback before that happens. In the meantime, I am correcting some glitches, updating a couple of other features, and maybe adding a dash of new content. There are going to be some [i]long[/i] patch notes in a few days =).

Thanks again, everyone!

notes.title: Update 2015.04.04: Happy Easter!
notes.content:
[img]http://i.imgur.com/duOwlBu.gif[/img]

I realize this might reach some regions too late to be much of an Easter surprise, but the good news is that you can easily enjoy this secular content (inspired by one of my favorite Easter/whenever films, Monty Python and the Holy Grail) year-round! The new prophecy requires the Balding Bomb and Holy Warriors packs to be completed, as well as the Lupine Lair be constructed.

Completing this prophecy unlocks a new artifact, the Glorious Grenade, which increases the potency of ALL explosions (even those delivered by your enemies) by one point. There is a new floor, the Rabid Rabbithole, which requires you to have the Lupine Lair AND this Grenade in your possession in order to build it--marking the first time an artifact enables a special floor. This floor produces Bloody Bunnies, which are adorable.

I hope you are all having a great holiday/regular weekend!

[h1]Changelog[/h1]
[b]Additions:[/b][list]
[*]Glorious Grenade--increase all explosive damage
[*]Rabid Rabbithole--gives Bloody Bunnies; requires Grenade and Lair
[*]Keyboard arrow key scrolling
[*]Character button scrolling with the mouse wheel (for when you have too many buttons to fit on screen at once)
[*]Ability for floors to require specific items in your inventory at construction time (you can discard the item after you build the floor)
[/list]
[b]Changes:[/b][list]
[*]Changed "Retreat" to "Withdraw" on menus, because I felt that sounded less cowardly and more villainous
[/list]
[b]Fixes:[/b][list]
[*]Added a fail-safe for combat stalls, so stuck battles should be jogged back into motion after a certain delay
[*]Corrected a couple of minion traits[/list]

notes.title: Update 2015.03.23: Guilty Guildhall
notes.content:
[img]http://i.imgur.com/81YjDVC.gif[/img]

Tonight's content is only sort of new, considering that the Guilty Guildhall is really just a new home for the existing thieves and sneaks. These two characters were the only examples of minions that were unlocked for an early floor by later floors, and I felt this was a bad precedent that would eventually only serve to complicate the build tree. As a result, they have been moved to a new home that requires either the Shady Shop or the Furtive Fence to build.

Also included in this update are a number of requested options (full screen, vsync, UI margin controls, no auto-pause on minimzation), as well as a balance change to production floors and fencing items: these will now deposit resources directly into your stockpile, rather than dropping tiles into the hoard.

This update also makes a lot of changes to UI width requirements; with the margin controls, it is now possible to fit the alternative floor UI and the dedicated hoard view on a 1080p display. If you previously had some overlap between UI elements, things should be a bit roomier now =).

Thanks for all of the reports and suggestions, everyone!

[h1]Changelog[/h1]
[b]Additions:[/b][list]
[*]Guilty Guildhall--produces Thieves (with Camp) and/or Goblin Sneaks (with Grotto)
[*]Full screen option (known bug: if you exit full screen mode, the window will be un-resizable until you restart the application; this is due to an engine bug that I cannot address until I return home next weekend--sorry!)
[*]VSync option (on by default)
[*]UI margin slider (margins are intended for TVs and other displays that require a title-safe region; previously, the maximum region was enforced)
[*]Pause on Focus Loss option (enabled by default; when disabled, the game will not automatically pause when the window looses focus)
[/list]
[b]Changes:[/b][list]
[*]Adjusted minimum width requirements for resolution scaling
[*]Default margins have been significantly reduced
[*]Production floors and fenced items now send resources directly to your collected stash and not the Hoard
[*]Production floors no longer produce the occasional item
[*]Removed dedicated glossary buttons during gameplay (and alternative codex location option) because these required an extra vertical column of space
[/list]
[b]Fixes:[/b][list]
[*]In the codex, floors could miscalculate that they were blocked from construction, when only one possible route was blocked--this did not affect whether the floors could actually be built[/list]

These two characters were the only examples of minions that were unlocked for an early floor by later floors, and I felt this was a bad precedent that would eventually only serve to complicate the build tree. As a result, they have been moved to a new home that requires either the Shady Shop or the Furtive Fence to build.

Also included in this update are a number of requested options (full screen, vsync, UI margin controls, no auto-pause on minimzation), as well as a balance change to production floors and fencing items: these will now deposit resources directly into your stockpile, rather than dropping tiles into the hoard.

This update also makes a lot of changes to UI width requirements; with the margin controls, it is now possible to fit the alternative floor UI and the dedicated hoard view on a 1080p display. If you previously had some overlap between UI elements, things should be a bit roomier now =).

Thanks for all of the reports and suggestions, everyone!

[h1]Changelog[/h1]
[b]Additions:[/b][list]
[*]Guilty Guildhall--produces Thieves (with Camp) and/or Goblin Sneaks (with Grotto)
[*]Full screen option (known bug: if you exit full screen mode, the window will be un-resizable until you restart the application; this is due to an engine bug that I cannot address until I return home next weekend--sorry!)
[*]VSync option (on by default)
[*]UI margin slider (margins are intended for TVs and other displays that require a title-safe region; previously, the maximum region was enforced)
[*]Pause on Focus Loss option (enabled by default; when disabled, the game will not automatically pause when the window looses focus)
[/list]
[b]Changes:[/b][list]
[*]Adjusted minimum width requirements for resolution scaling
[*]Default margins have been significantly reduced
[*]Production floors and fenced items now send resources directly to your collected stash and not the Hoard
[*]Production floors no longer produce the occasional item
[*]Removed dedicated glossary buttons during gameplay (and alternative codex location option) because these required an extra vertical column of space
[/list]
[b]Fixes:[/b][list]
[*]In the codex, floors could miscalculate that they were blocked from construction, when only one possible route was blocked--this did not affect whether the floors could actually be built[/list]

notes.title: Update 2015.03.12: Suave Scoundrels
notes.content:
[img]http://i.imgur.com/mQk4daP.gif[/img]
It's a boy! As I've mentioned probably too often for official posts, my wife and I had been expecting, and last week, she gave birth right here at home to our first child, Atlas. It's been an amazing week, despite the near-sleepless nights and the practically progress-free days. To celebrate our new son, I whipped up a pack of Suave Scoundrels (the alternative, daughter-inspired Femme Fatale pack will have to wait for another time--though probably not for an actual daughter =)).

Included in this update is the dissolution of the "hunter" minion type. I finally decided to just make all of the patrolling AI smarter (rather than just predictable), so now patrolling behavior includes some of the hunter logic; minions will attempt to cut off heroes that slip by. I actually rewrote large amounts of AI while making this change, so we may need to keep an eye on its performance.

There are also a number of UI adjustments and improvements, as well as a bunch of groundwork being laid for some upcoming features.

Speaking of which, if you would like to help test some potential major mechanical changes, here's a thread on how you can help: http://steamcommunity.com/app/340360/discussions/0/610575007204564803/

I'm sorry for the relatively huge delay between updates this time (ten whole days!), but things are finally starting to calm back down, so I should be slowly returning to the more regular update regimen I had been keeping up.

[h1]Changelog[/h1]
[b]Additions:[/b][list]
[*]Suave Scoundrels hero pack: Human Musketeer, Elven Bard, and Dwarven Privateer--build the Turncloak Tavern to discover their prophecy
[*]All minimap floor highlights are now also applied to the outlines of floors in the dungeon view[/list]

[b]Changes:[/b][list]
[*]Folded "hunter" AI into the "patrol" AI, and eliminated "hunters"; AI should generally be more intelligent about tracking down heroes that have slipped by, instead of just blindly patrolling all of the time
[*]Lots of internal changes to prophecy handling, in preparation for future, non-prophecy objectives
[*]When dragging or hovering over items, the variable floor highlights are more drastic than before
[*]Moved ritual count to right side
[*]Scaled purchase button brightness with number of units on offer
[*]The usual batch of other minor UI adjustments[/list]

[b]Fixes:[/b][list]
[*]Some small errors and shortcomings in the character animation system
[*]Champion projectile attacks were sometimes launching from the champion portrait rather than from the character itself[/list]

notes.title: Update 2015.03.02--Portable Punji
notes.content:
[img]http://i.imgur.com/3dNrhDS.gif[/img]
[Edit: Uploaded 2015.03.02b to add a few minor fixes and adjustments; notes below.]

This update contains a few fixes and adjustments, as well as one new item: the Portable Punji trap. Now you can deploy a single-use spike trap on any floor you see fit =)!

[h1]Changelog[/h1]
[b]Additions:[/b][list]
[*]Portable Punji--deployable spike trap deals three melee damage to all enemies when triggered. I suggest building some later kobold floors to unlock it.
[*]A flee cooldown has been added to champions; while fleeing, they will avoid fights for three floors before they return to normal duty
[*]A proper window icon, replacing the standard libGDX one
[*](2015.03.02b)"Send to back" functionality for prophecy pop-ups; this second button works the way the old close button used to work for prophecy pop-ups, and the close button now actually closes the prophecy window
[/list]

[b]Changes:[/b][list]
[*]I made a few improvements to patrol AI which should result in avoiding floors that are full and reacting to access changes a little more consistently
[*]Slightly reduced several unit prices
[*]Of course, more small UI adjustments (raised message log, scooted over the ritual count a little, added another status to the champion display, etc.)
[*](2015.03.02b)Recruitment prophecy goals are now more lenient; for example, if it says "recruit X goblins," anything with "goblin" in the name counts, not just regular goblins--same for kobolds, gremlins, etc.[/list]

[b]Fixes:[/b][list]
[*]Addressed a glitch and potential crash caused by making the last minion flee a battle
[*]Corrected inconsistencies in prophecy goals caused by resetting stats
[*]The arrows along the dedicated hoard view can now be used to grab a row, the same as the arrows along the actual hoard
[*](2015.03.02b)Fixed message log sizing issues with certain messages
[*](2015.03.02b)Fixed death skull/smoke appearing in the wrong location sometimes
[/list]

notes.title: Update 2015.02.27--Achievements and OS X
notes.content:
[Edit 2: Uploaded 2015.02.28 to address inadvertently broken progress on the floor-building achievement (Starter Stronghold), increase difficulty of the Cheapskate Challenge achievement (increasing wave goal from 15 to 20--I made it to 25 in my first attempt, but I decided not to set the goal quite that high), and adjust a couple of the recent UI changes. Thanks!]

[Edit: Made a small adjustment to configuration that was preventing this update from running for many players. Apologies for any inconvenience!]

Here's the first batch of 16 achievements; it's a range of the usual fare (unlock some stuff, build some things) with a dash of the weird (score a Tyrant kill or stockpile 50 of a single resource). As the game grows, I'll release additional batches of achievements that leverage that growth, and which probably fall a little more on the weird end of the spectrum.

I've also officially added OS X support to the game. Steam has technically hosted an OS X version of the game since launch, but I have held off on adding official support until I could have more people verify that the distributables I've been creating actually work on OS X, as I am unable to test this for myself. While I have had one user report a problem, I have also had a few inform me that the game is running fine, so I am choosing to make it available now and field any future issues one-on-one to improve stability going forward.

Sorry for the delay between updates and the relatively short feature list this time around, but I've had a stressful week, led by my over-adventurous (and overdue) unborn child going breech, thwarting our home-birth plans and culminating in a crazy baby-flipping procedure, which was conducted in a for-reals hospital, but was apparently inspired by a shamanistic blend of Gaelic druidery and ancient Eastern mysticism. It was pretty cool, but draining and worrisome, all the same. We are thankfully back on track for our home-birth; the baby may come at any time now, and then things will surely calm down.  Right?

Thanks for all of the reports, achievement input, and generally awesome support, everyone!

[b]Fixes:[/b][list]

notes.title: Update 2015.02.21--Champion Control
notes.content:
[img]http://i.imgur.com/AosZmOx.gif[/img]
[Edit: Uploaded 2015.02.21b to address a new crash.]

This update adds something that could be a game-changer and may require some additional balancing and expansion: champion control! Your champion minions will now be displayed above the hoard view, and you can station them on floors by dragging and dropping them on the map (or minimap). Clicking their stationed icon will have them revert from defending that floor to doing their own thing.

They can also be ordered to flee from a battle by clicking their little activity icon, but doing so will prevent them from rejoining that encounter later. Incidentally, Dropping items on their icon will have the same effect as dropping that item on their current floor.

[h1]Changelog[/h1]
[b]Additions:[/b][list]
[*]Champion UI elements
[*]Champions can be stationed on floors
[*]Champions can retreat from battle to fight another day
[*]Faint background for tooltips, to increase contrast between tooltips and other elements[/list]

[b]Changes:[/b][list]
[*]Players are only allowed 24 champions (still quite a lot)
[*]Several small adjustments to tooltips for items and other elements[/list]

[b]Fixes:[/b][list]
[*]Corrected a number of animation and texture glitches on floors and previews
[*]Floor UI pricing tooltips were visible when available floor previews were not

notes.title: 2015.02.17--Item Tooltips
notes.content:
[img]http://i.imgur.com/r2IiARW.png[/img]

[Uploaded 2015.02.19 to address a shader error that caused the game to crash on stricter video cards.]

Tonight's update is relatively minor, with a couple requested features and several minor changes and fixes. Item tooltips are the most obvious addition; when dragging an item over a floor (or on the minimap), you'll see dynamic tooltips that tell you the effect of dropping that item on that floor. This is a pretty simplified list of effects for now, with some room for future improvements later.

Additionally, on the minimap, you'll see varying floor highlights that indicate the potency of using the current item on each floor, so you can make snap judgments in potion placement.

I would normally hold off on updating for such seemingly minor things, but the next wave of big stuff could be a little longer, and I also wanted to push through some of these bug fixes. Furthermore, I've got a baby due any day now, and who knows how that will complicate my schedule!

[h1]Changelog[/h1]
[b]Additions:[/b][list]
[*]Tooltips while dragging items over floors
[*]Support for icons in tooltips (used for the above, and possibly some future things)
[/list]

[b]Changes:[/b][list]
[*]Disabled pitch changes to background music. This was a cheap way to increase the tempo, but the changes were jarring and grating, so I'll explore another avenue for intensifying music at a later date
[*]Improved minimap item use highlighting (both its internal accuracy, and also in how it displays use potency)
[*]Poison damage is now also dealt when a character changes floors; previously, this damage only occurred when a character ended a combat turn, but now, poisoned heroes will take damage as they continue their descent
[*]Afraid characters now reduce fear as they descend as well
[*]Adjusted highlight shades used on some tiles[/list]

[b]Fixes:[/b][list]
[*]Tooltips were rendering behind the minimap
[*]Some resource icons (Fence sales message, floor production) weren't being colored by the new system
[*]Fixed a mistake on the Tyrant's codex page[/list]

notes.title: 2015.02.16--Color Control
notes.content:
[img]http://i.imgur.com/k3ANpps.png[/img]

I've finally added some colorblindness support to the game, in the form of near complete control over the eight resource colors used throughout the game. And if you aren't colorblind, you can still adjust them however you see fit; like pastels? grayscale?, or maybe you just prefer your flesh well-done? Go for it.

The current limitations are that many items use secondary colors or bright highlights that may look out of place, and you are prevented from selecting very dark colors, as that doesn't play nicely with UI elements that have to match your selected colors.

I would like to provide a good colorblindness profile so players don't have to create it themselves; if anyone can send or post a screenshot of a profile that they think works well for this (a single screenshot of the options menu, which displays all of the resource icons, is sufficient), I can sample your colors and work that into the game as a single option, to save others time =).

Thanks to a generous and talented member of our Steam community, Tom Paine, there is also a new chiptune-inspired music track to try out in the options (track 7). It is not in the regular rotation, but give it a listen and let me know what you think.

[h1]Changelog[/h1]
[b]Additions:[/b][list]
[*]Color controls
[*]Alternative codex position in options (similar to before the hoard view)
[*]One new music track (#7)[/list]

[b]Changes:[/b][list]
[*]Slight adjustments to default resource colors
[*]The tyrant is now listed in the Codex character glossary[/list]

[b]Fixes:[/b][list]

notes.title: 2015.02.16--Color Control
notes.content:
[img]http://i.imgur.com/k3ANpps.png[/img]

I've finally added some colorblindness support to the game, in the form of near complete control over the eight resource colors used throughout the game. And if you aren't colorblind, you can still adjust them however you see fit; like pastels? grayscale?, or maybe you just prefer your flesh well-done? Go for it.

The current limitations are that many items use secondary colors or bright highlights that may look out of place, and you are prevented from selecting very dark colors, as that doesn't play nicely with UI elements that have to match your selected colors.

I would like to provide a good colorblindness profile so players don't have to create it themselves; if anyone can send or post a screenshot of a profile that they think works well for this (a single screenshot of the options menu, which displays all of the resource icons, is sufficient), I can sample your colors and work that into the game as a single option, to save others time =).

Thanks to a generous and talented member of our Steam community, Tom Paine, there is also a new chiptune-inspired music track to try out in the options (track 7). It is not in the regular rotation, but give it a listen and let me know what you think.

[h1]Changelog[/h1]
[b]Additions:[/b][list]
[*]Color controls
[*]Alternative codex position in options (similar to before the hoard view)
[*]One new music track (#7)[/list]

[b]Changes:[/b][list]
[*]Slight adjustments to default resource colors
[*]The tyrant is now listed in the Codex character glossary[/list]

[b]Fixes:[/b][list]
[*]Volume option displays were broken
[*]Music track preferences weren't saving immediately
[*]Prophecy completion discrepancy, when an update changes the goals of a previously completed prophecy (prophecy should remain completed)[/list]

notes.title: Update 2015.02.05--Barren Barrows
notes.content:
[img]http://i.imgur.com/ygb8AQr.gif[/img]

I heard some of you would appreciate more undead, so here's the Barren Barrows, a home for Ghouls (with goblins) and Wyrmbone Wights (with kobolds). The ghouls deal ice damage and generate fear. The Wights are undead kobolds, with the same stats as the living--except kobold bones are as strong as their draconic ancestors, so these wights are immune to mundane physical damage (melee and ranged). They are otherwise rather weak--like kobolds--and the number of heroes with non-physical attacks is increasing, so I think this will balance out.

There are also some fixes and adjustments for the UI changes in yesterday's update.

[h1]Changelog[/h1]
[b]Additions:[/b][list]
[*]Barren Barrows (requires Bonehoard+Grotto or Bonehoard+Warrens)--unlocks Ghouls and Wights
[/list]

[b]Changes:[/b][list]
[*]Adjusted a couple of UI elements and view center slightly
[/list]

[b]Fixes:[/b][list]
[*]Could interact with floor UI while it was covered
[*]Item colors weren't swapping on buttons or in the codex
[*]Codex glossary buttons could obstruct purchase buttons
[*]Some codex click hitboxes were too large
[/list]

notes.title: Update 2015.02.04--Holy Warriors
notes.content:
[img]http://i.imgur.com/7O6VCMT.gif[/img]

First off, the dedicated hoard view is now on by default, and there have been a bunch of UI adjustments to accommodate this at different resolutions. Let me know how you feel about the new layout, because if people seem okay with it, I will probably keep it this way for the foreseeable future, and move on to updating controller support and such.

All of the game's collectible tiles and items have been changed over to the color-swapping system, so you'll notice some palette changes, because they are now drawn in primary colors rather than their final colors. This is the first step toward allowing players to adjust resource colors to suit their preferences or needs (for color-blind players); you can't change the colors yet, but the groundwork is there.

I've also added a new pack of heroes: a Human Paladin, a Human Monk, and a Dwarven Cleric. They all deal holy damage (so your undead and demons should watch out), and the latter two have some healing abilities.

[h1]Changelog[/h1]
[b]Additions:[/b][list]
[*]Holy Warriors hero pack (Human Paladin, Human Monk, and Dwarven Cleric)
[/list]

[b]Changes:[/b][list]
[*]All tiles moved over to color-swapping
[*]Several UI elements have been rearranged (most noticeably, the minimap and meters)
[/list]

[b]Fixes:[/b][list]
[*]Multipliers weren't rendering on the hoard view
[*]Damage weakness was sometimes not behaving as intended (one point of damage should always get through)
[*]Prophecy messages weren't updating the message log height properly, causing single messages to sometimes render partially off-screen
[*]When watching the surface, champion stars could render over the hoard view
[*]Corrected a few glitches in floor and character graphics
[/list]

notes.title: Update 2015.01.30--Oppressive Overlook
notes.content:
[img]http://i.imgur.com/mrErXc5.gif[/img]

This update brings an optional dedicated hoard UI. This is still kind of experimental so I have disabled it by default. This default will probably change in a future update, but for now, you will have to enable it from the options menu.

notes.title: Update 2015.01.26--New Floor-Building UI
notes.content:
[img]http://i.imgur.com/QMTxPzc.gif[/img]

This update adds a new floor-building UI, replacing the vertical line of floor buttons on the left side of the dungeon with images that appear between the Sanctum and the tile queue (or whatever you want to call that bar that briefly catches falling tiles). The goal was to create something much more compact than the old buttons; while fun, the buttons occupied a lot of space and were overlapped by other UI. I am sure the new UI will go through some revisions, as well (perhaps a brief indicator that floors are available when the UI itself is not visible).

The old UI remains accessible in the options menu, under "Legacy Floor UI," in case there are problems with the new layout, and I appreciate any feedback on this change!

I also added a batch of Gnomish heroes to face: an engineer, a heavy, and a demoma--demolitions expert. You might notice a theme here and expect a continuation of it down the road =).

[h1]Changelog[/h1]

[b]Additions:[/b][list]
[*]New floor-building UI
[*]"Defensive" Gnomes: engineer, heavy, and demo
[*]Additional shader capabilities
[/list]

[b]Changes:[/b][list]
[*]Altered tooltip display rules a little, so mouse-over text is less likely to display on a "bad" side of the cursor
[*]Some small codex formatting changes
[*]New floors now spawn in below the Sanctum and are swapped upward
[*]Codex has been pushed up a bit, and the message log expanded
[/list]

[b]Fixes:[/b][list]
[*]A couple of longstanding shader bugs regarding floor rendering
[*]Potion buffs applied outside of battle could be lost before the unit entered a conflict, wasting the potion
[/list]

notes.title: Update 2015.01.15b--Rituals
notes.content:
[Edit: Uploaded 2015.01.15c to fix bombs and improve floor recommendations for items]

Reintroducing: rituals! Rituals were the original plan for unlocking new content (instead of prophecies), but prophecies are better, so rituals got nixed--pretty much right before Early Access began.

Rituals are target arrangements of tiles, and this update brings rituals back in a different capacity; completing rituals by matching tiles to the ritual's shape will now earn you resource pool size bonuses, so your maximum assets will increase over the course of a game.

I've also added a new leaderboard for tracking players who have completed the most rituals in a single game. Have at it!

[h1]Changelog[/h1]
[b]Additions:[/b][list]
[*]Rituals
[*]Ritual leaderboard
[*]Ability to use items on a floor by dragging them over the minimap
[/list]
[b]Fixes:[/b][list]
[*]Purchase buttons were not updating position consistently after resource changes
[*]Using a balding bomb would exhaust the entire stack
[/list]
